recs.name: South Wall
recs.tag: The whimpering of conscience is drowned out by the clanging of gold and silver in the bowl.

lines.x: Morning, Hung. Day off?
Hehe, something came up, so I had to call out.
Are you sick? You should go home and rest!
Nah, it's not that.
So, how's your new job going?
(Whisper) Shh! That look on his face, I bet he got fired again.
(Whisper) Again? How many times has that been...? Kid's too nice and doesn't know how to be flexible.
(Whisper) You've got to be clever to make it these days.
(Whisper) Yeah, got to move with the times.
What did I tell you when you first showed up? Don't poke your nose where it doesn't belong!
Looks like you spent so much time at the top that your brain got addled from the lack of oxygen.
You gotta be flexible if you wanna do business in Lungmen!
You have any idea how much work it took to get this batch of goods?
And you threw it all out, just because you weren't sure of the source! Thank you very much, Mister Avatar of Justice!
Boss, this stuff's dangerous... what if it gets into the hands of the mafia?
Who cares as long as they pay in gold and silver? Who do you think you are, trying to teach me how to do business?
But...
But what? No buts. Get out, and don't let me see your face again.
Sorry, boss, I just...
Get out! You're just like your dad. He deserved to be broke, and you deserve to be out on the street!
Boss, this has nothing to do with my dad...
GET LOST!
(Rumble—)
(Sigh... I should get something to eat, then I can think about what to do next.)
Grand opening! 20% off during the opening promotion! Don't miss your chance to taste authentic Shangshu home cooking!
(Reaches for the wallet)
I think I have enough. Let's go.
Welcome! What can I get you?
Er, let me look at the menu.
How about our signature item the 'Full House?' A set of meat and vegetable toppings. It's really great!
Thanks, but I'll just have a bowl of plain noodles.
Just plain noodles? No drink, no sides?
No, thanks. Just plain noodles.
Hmph. Fine, take a number and get in line.
...Thanks.
I'm looking to get a small bowl of noodles... any recommendations for a first timer?
That would be our signature 'Full House.' Everyone loves it!
Sure, I'll take it.
Now that's what I like to hear. Here's your number, and I'll have it to you in a jiffy.
Alright then, thanks.
Hey, buddy, have you eaten here before? What do you think?
No, this is my first time.
Ever had Shangshu food before?
I had some when I was little, at a big restaurant with my dad. I loved it.
Haha. Bigger isn't always better when it comes to restaurants.
Here's your noodles, sir. Would love to hear your thoughts afterwards, good or bad.
Sure thing.
Excuse me, what about mine...?
You can't rush things, you know. Noodles take time.
But this gentleman's are ready. Why are mine taking longer?
What are you talking about? You didn't order the same type.
Young people these days have no patience. Good food takes time!
Ahem. Probably shouldn't keep your customers waiting, friend. You just opened, after all.
Huh? Oh, yeah, you're right, enjoy your meal.
(Nods in gratitude)
Haha, don't mention it.
Phew...
(I guess I can wait a little longer.)
(The interior of this place looks pretty nice. I guess this is the Shangshu style.)
(When I was little, dad said we would go to Shangshu and really dig into the local cuisine... bah, no use thinking about it when he's not around anymore.)
(Hey, why is that guy peeking left and right?)
(He took out a paper packet... Wait, did he just pinch something into the bowl?)
Hey, what are you doi—
Hey, boss, what's going on here?!
Is there a problem, sir?
There's a bug in this bowl! Look, a huge one, black and shiny.
That's impossible. I hold myself to the highest standard of cleanliness.
Talk all you want! I got proof floating right there in this bowl!
What are you trying to pull?! I've got cameras watching the shop, they'll prove you're just looking for trouble.
(Flips over the table) Huh? You want a fight?
Busy with their argument, neither party notices that the bowl of noodles, which was launched into the air with the table, is headed straight for Lee.
Hm?
(No rush. I can dodge it after another bite.)
Ow, it burns!
Are you ok, sir? Did any of the soup hit you?
I'm fine. You got a faceful of the hot noodle soup, though. Here, use this handkerchief.
(Ack, I guess I owe him one now.)
Thank you.
Hung shakes off the pieces of noodles and vegetables on his face, then wipes it with the handkerchief.
He holds the soiled cloth in his hand, not sure what to do. He looks over to Lee, seeing him point to the top of his head.
There's still something there.
Hung scratches his head, feels something hard in the fur, and pulls out a big, black, shiny bug.
You want a beating, huh?
H-Hey, what are you doing?
I'm not playing word games with you anymore. The fist talks louder!
Alright, I won't charge you for the noodles. How about that?
Are you kidding me? You think one bowl of noodles is gonna do it?
Let... let me go, I can't breathe...
You—
You heard him? Let him go!
And who do think you are? Go eat your noodles and stop poking your nose where it doesn't belong.
Didn't you hear him? Let. Him. Go.
Looks like you want a beating too, eh?
I... I'm sorry, it's all my fault, I won't do it again... please, let me go...
Could you stop crying? You make it sound like I'm bullying you.
(I hit him harder than I meant to. I hope he's okay...)
Are you gonna be alright? Do you need a doctor?
(No way he really cares! He's making sure that I won't spill the beans on him!)
Are... you alright?
I-I'm fine, I just fell down on my own, nothing to do with you at all, not a thing!
Er... fell down? I thought I...
No, you weren't even there, don't worry, it's all my fault for being so clumsy, haha...
I-I gotta go, bye!
You're limping... just be careful, don't try to run too fast.
Thank you very much! Small businesses like ours always have a hard time.
You're not hurt, are you?
Not at all, thanks to you.
(Rumble—)
Er, sorry, but... are my noodles ready yet?
Oh, how silly of me! Take a seat, and I'll be right up with your order.
Thanks, kid. A certain little girl would've chewed my head off if I went home with soiled clothes.
You have a daughter, sir?
Not exactly... well, I guess daughter's the best way to put it.
Oh? What do you mean?
It's a long story... say, you have some good moves. Who did you study with?
I'm nothing special, just learned a couple things from my dad.
I remember there was a guy who owned a security firm who used the same grappling technique. His surname escapes me at the moment...
Ko. That's my father.
Yeah, that's it! How is he?
He passed away last year.
Ah... I'm sorry to hear that.
It's all in the past now, but thanks for the kind words.
Here's your noodles, sir. I added a bit of meat broth for you, a touch of extra flavor.
Oh... thank you.
(Picks up chopsticks)
Now...
(Puts down chopsticks) Is there something you wanted to say, sir?
Well, you know, rent around here is high, and businesses are always barely scraping by.
Yes, I know...
Sure, chasing away that hoodlum was a big help, but you also made a mess of the place while you were at it.
We ought to keep it separate, no? The noodles are for helping me out, which is one thing.
And the other?
About the mess you made... surely it's fair to ask that you pay for repairs?
(Tightens fist) I was only trying to help you...
Hey now, what's with the fist?
You're gonna punch me? Looks like you're no better than that hoodlum, pushing people around just because you know kung fu.
No... I didn't mean to...
Then pay up!
Sir, you shouldn't do this... it's not right...
What do you mean not right? Break something, pay for it. It's the proper way to do things.
You only took a couple of bites, dad... you're not gonna get better like this.
Oh, don't you worry. The guy in the next bed over already laughs at me for how over-protective my son is... *cough*, *cough*.
Well, you shouldn't laugh with him, the way your lungs are. Anything else you want to eat? I can slice another apple for you. Hard to sleep on an empty stomach, after all.
It's been a long time since I've had fried rice.
Not sure that's a good idea. It'll give you indigestion and keep you up all night.
Worrying again. I was just kidding, Fine, fine, slice me up an apple.
Alright...
How's working coming along? Has Old Li been yelling at you?
It's going great. Uncle Li says I've got a great attitude.
Who do you think you're fooling? That long look on your face, I bet you got a good chewing out. No need to hide things from your dad, tell me the truth.
Well... I got into an argument with Uncle Li. It's just not fair for him to mistreat his customers like that over a few coins.
Sigh, you're just like me, always so stubborn about doing the right thing. I paid my price; don't be like me.
Why do you say that? You've always taught me right and wrong.
And look where it got me! You're barely twenty, with your whole life ahead of you. No need to get yourself bruised and battered like me.
What are you talking about, dad?!
Listen to your father, Hei-sing. Sometimes, you have to let it go rather than banging your head against it forever.
Daydreaming, kid? Like I said, the bill's fifteen thousand. How do you want to pay?
(Loosens fist)
...I don't have a lot of money on me. Can I pay it by helping out around the shop?
Ha, sure, wouldn't hurt to have some free labor. I'm sure you can put those muscles to use washing dishes. Meals and bed not included, just to be clear.
I'm done eating. I'll leave the cash here.
Thank you! Have a pleasant day, sir.
Oh, you said you wanted my thoughts, didn't you? Actually, I just found a big problem that I'd better share.
Appreciate it, sir, but I'm a little busy right now.
Sure, I can wait. Not sure if you can though.
Er... well, what is it, sir?
I was counting your fire extinguishers here while I was eating. I saw three.
But if I'm not mistaken, we got some new regs last month that require a minimum of six for an establishment of this size, with a five thousand dollar fine per missing piece.
Let me run the numbers here real quick... comes out to fifteen thousand.
The fire department's really cracking down on this stuff lately. One call, and the fire marshal's here in minutes. I do wonder if you'd have the time to sort things out.
That sure is a pickle, isn't it?
No need to beat around the bush, sir.
Given that you just opened, I think you should probably let it go. Trouble's bad for business.
So you're here to play nice guy, eh? Don't you have better things to do than stick your nose where it doesn't belong?
Oh, but I think my nose very much belongs here. Fire safety is the responsibility of each and every Lungmen citizen, after all.
You... how dare you...?
Fine, fine, whatever! Forget it, just get out, both of you!
You heard the man. Let's go.
Thank you so much for helping me out, sir. I'm not sure how to repay your kindness, but if you ever need a pair of strong hands, I'm happy to help.
Ha, don't mention it. All I did was say a few words.
S-Sir!
Really, there's no need to thank me.
N-No, it's not that.
Is there something else?
Could you... could you teach me?
Teach you? What could I possibly teach you?
I used to believe that right and wrong were as clear as black and white.
But now, thinking back on things, I see only gray; where white ends and black starts, I just can't tell.
Oh? And why is that?
There are so many people here in Lungmen. People looking for money, for justice, for life, for fun, for fame, for the truth... they all gather here.
Everyone has a different story, and everyone has their own ideas of right and wrong.
When one person's right is another's wrong, they resort to violence and force their ideas on each other.
What's right and wrong? Where's justice and fairness?
Teach me what you know, sir. I don't want to keep banging my head until I bleed, but I also don't want to bow down to anyone.
You're still young. It's natural you feel lost.
But I can't teach you what you want to know...
I'm just one of the many people here in Lungmen, after all.
Sir, I...
(Rumble—)
...But maybe I can teach you something else. Like how to make fried rice that tastes just right.
Fried rice?
Yeah. How about it?
I... Yes. Thank you, sir.
Let's go, then. We can get some spring onions and eggs from the market on the way.

recs.name: Conspiracy
recs.tag: Hung knows that there are many things for which there is no possibility of reparation. But he continues to believe that there is a way, as long as people continue to communicate and try to understand each other.

lines.x: No, you don't understand. If this goes on...
I-I could very well find myself killed!
Wha?
Have you tried the cops?

*sigh* Of course I have. They said I'm just overthinking it. I asked around and someone told me about you guys. You're a detective agency, right? Figuring out who wants to kill me and making sure I'm safe should be right up your alley!
Besides, I'm pretty sure... the L.G.D. are actually working with those guys.
That's gotta be why they're ignoring me!

Oh? The L.G.D.'s in on it, you say?
Alright, interesting. We'll take the case!
Normally, we charge a thousand LMD per billable hour, but I'll give you a discount. 30 thousand for the whole job. How's that?
Wait, slow down there, Aak.
(Whispers) Look, I'm sick of eating nothing but cup noodles every single day. Which of the gigs you picked up lately even got us paid, anyway? At this rate, we'll be dead before Lee's back.
And please calm down a little, Mr... uh...
Hung looks down at the business card he got from the man earlier. He works for a famous corporation in Lungmen, with a fairly impressive title next to his name to boot.
Hung thinks to himself, the client probably has much more lavish meals than cup noodles every day.
Mr. Lau.
You said earlier that you think you're being followed. Are you sure you are not imagining things?
For example, a few days ago I was at the wet markets picking up groceries, and I was certain someone was following me... until I realized it was just a cloudbeast cub.
I'm telling you, it's not like that! Look...
Mr. Lau cautiously looks around.
Lately, there've been all these strange marks on the walls outside my front door. I looked it up on the intercity net! They all say it means somebody's out to get me!
And I actually felt some strange glances! Both during my commute and even at the office! It always feels like there's somebody observing me.
Ugh... Just thinking about it gives me chills.
Look, maybe it's just a stray cloudbeast...
Why would there be a stray cloudbeast in an office building?!
And scariest of all is that I keep hearing someone whispering at night...
Mr. Lau, at the end of the street, you'll find a store that sells essential oils. There's this oil with a calming effect that I've tried out. It really helps give you sleep better.
Maybe you're just a little tense lately. Try massaging yourself with some of that oil. It'll calm you down.
*sigh* Not you too...
But you know, it does sound like somebody might be following him.
You don't just constantly feel like somebody's watching you for no reason.
And speaking from experience, if you can notice them at all, it just shows how fearless they are. They aren't afraid of being seen, much less what you'd do after you find out.
Right?!
Hey now, stop scaring the client. This is nothing like that. Your situation's... a lot more unique.
By the way, Mr. Lau, are the marks still there?
Yeah, you bet they are! I wiped them off once, but then they showed up again, and I didn't dare wipe them off again... On top of that, they keep multiplying every few days.
Then let's go have a look right now.
Now?
When else? If I were the mastermind behind this, I'd definitely be watching him in the dead of night.
Hung looks at the time displayed on his terminal and scratches his head.
We don't even know if there's actually a mastermind per se...
But alright. Mr. Lau, would you mind if we go have a look now? Maybe it could offer you some peace of mind.
N-Not at all!
Hold up, let me bring my camera!
As the sparse traffic speeds down the road, the streetlights lining the sidewalks light up one after another. Mr. Lau is walking in front of the two investigators, looking back from time to time.
What? You think someone's following you again?
I don't feel them now. Weird... I was sure somebody was watching me on my way to your office...
Maybe you're just a little too nervous. The old man at the canteen downstairs loves to watch people come and go when he's got nothing to do. He probably just thought you looked a little strange.
I-Is that so...
Oh, here we are. My flat is here, up on the second floor.
Mr. Lau's home is in an old shopping district. The mottled coating on the outer wall is starting to peel off, and there is a damp stench in the staircase.

Fearfully, he points at the walls by his front door. There are indeed multiple strange marks. One is particularly evident, with three more slender traces criss-crossing each other and leading toward the door.
Look, right here! I wiped them off before, then a couple days later, they showed up again. The same pattern, too. Always the same pattern...
The spacing's consistent, but the depth's different... Doesn't look manmade—
Is it a ghost, then?!
More like they were made by machines.
Mr. Lau, whoever's behind this, looks like they brought a machine to spook you.
Wh-What...
Hung crouches down and observes the wall. He lightly touches the dust on the ground and rubs it between his fingers, revealing a faint light-blue gleam.
Aak starts to take pictures of the wall, as Hung turns around toward the staircase.
It's a false alarm, Mr. Lau. This wasn't drawn deliberately. The faint light-blue powder here is just dried soap.
And considering the pattern in the spacing... this is probably from a cleaning robot.
How can you be so sure?
There are tread marks. Look.
Aak and Mr. Lau look toward where Hung is pointing, and see faint tread marks on the floor beneath the marks on the wall.
Uh, you sure? Maybe the culprit rode one of those little scooters here to mark his walls.
H-Huh?
It's okay, Mr. Lau. The marks are likely just a misunderstanding. Now how about we figure out what the whispers you heard at night were? Do you mind if we go inside?
P-Please, by all means!
(Whispers) But I heard somebody running away when I opened the door yesterday... Was that the janitor?
The night is deep. Mr. Lau's home is lit by only a few small lights. Through the window blinds, the red light of the neon signs outside can be seen flashing.
Hung stays at the door to check if there is any moment outside as Aak looks out the window, pointing a flashlight at the building across the street and occasionally taking pictures with his camera.

Meanwhile, Mr. Lau has wrapped himself up in a blanket, with a flashlight clenched tightly in his hand. The only thing that can be heard inside the room is the faint sound of the breeze, interrupted intermittently by the shutter of Aak's camera.
Doesn't look like anyone passed outside. I can just barely hear cars speeding past and nothing else. Aak, what are you looking at over there?
You know, the folks in this neighborhood all seem pretty nice. There's even somebody downstairs feeding a stray cloudbeast at this hour.
Say, do you think anyone'd come feed us if we went downstairs and lied down on the ground at night?
Looks like he's done feeding it. The cloudbeast cub is coming this way now... Oh, look at it hop. What a lively one.

Let me take a picture...
No, that can't be a stray. Look, it's got a collar.
Oh, that's Siumi. Probably a pet that got lost. You can always find someone feeding it these days.
It's pretty friendly, too. Every night, it comes up to my window for a walk. Wait, why are we talking about cloudbeasts?
Just wait a little longer. Every night around this time, you can hear these strange whispers coming from the wall...
Bzz—zzz—
Right after he finishes his sentence, the room falls silent for a brief moment, before the gang actually hears a strange noise.
Th-That's the sound!
It sounds like some kinda current to me...

Mr. Lau is so anxious that he begins to sweat. Aak finds himself bewildered, too. On the other hand, Hung's usual cool composure remains unchanged. He stands up slowly, and presses his ear against the wall for a few seconds. Then, he heads toward the kitchen.
After a few minutes, the sound dissipates.
Huh? The sound of the current stopped. What did you just do?
That was the air purifier. There was something stuck inside, and I pulled it out.
The fan's a little loose, and it got stuck inside the machine when it was turning. That's why it was making all that noise. Maybe it only sounded like voices because it's in the other room.
That's it? What was stuck inside anyway?
Looks like some kind of component.

It's been some time since I used it, actually. But since the air quality in town's been pretty bad lately, I've been keeping it on to at least get some fresher air inside the place, and it hasn't been turned off the entire time. Never thought something could be stuck inside...
Oh, maybe it fell inside when that plumber came to fix the pipes last week? I knew it... The plumbers on the intercity net are all unreliable... That's what I get for being cheap.
This part...
*sigh* Good thing I had you two come check this out for me. If it weren't for you, I probably wouldn't be able to live here anymore.
You're just too on edge. Calm down. Lungmen isn't full of conspiracies, and there's no such thing as ghosts.

You've been imagining things because of all these strange marks and sounds, and I can sympathize with that, but you seem overly nervous. I hope you don't mind me asking, but did something happen recently?

If you ask me, given that you think someone's been following you, and that you're even worried about threats to your life... there has to be something more than the marks on the wall and the air purifier's sounds that got you so worried in the first place.
Uhh...
To tell you the truth, I actually... reported a coworker from my company last week... for smuggling and embezzlement.
I've always known that the company deals in some pretty shady business, and that coworker of mine keeps getting promoted pretty quickly, so I suspected him... No, I guess I just envied him...
But I got so hotheaded that I went and reported him! Ever since, I've been scared he'll come and get me.
And I haven't seen him in the office all week, either... Maybe... Maybe he's making preparations to off me.
Why didn't you tell us sooner?!
Misunderstandings between people ought to be resolved as soon as possible. Otherwise, they'll start piling up, and things are bound to get out of hand from there.
It's pretty late already, so we'll head back for the day. Calm down. Everything will be resolved by the time you visit our office tomorrow.
Oh, thank you so much, you two! As for your payment—
Let's not get ahead of ourselves. We'll talk about that tomorrow. Try to get some rest now.
Interesting. Someone's out to get revenge, huh?
And how can you be so sure that you'll have this taken care of by tomorrow?
Well, it's just a little misunderstanding. I can handle that.

Once we get paid tomorrow, we'll finally be able to get ourselves some fresh vegetables. Stir-fried meat with corn, braised ribs with pumpkin, and how about some cucumber salad with cloud ears? Anything you want to eat, Aak?
Come on, I'm just asking you to come up with a dish for dinner tomorrow. No need to look all serious.

You know, I'm really not sure about this. There's no way that Siumi just so happens to take leisurely walks on his windowsill every single night, and there just so happen to be strange sounds that start as soon as it makes its way up.
Check out the tag on its collar! It glows! Look, I got a picture here. Just think about it. Why would anyone give a cloudbeast that kinda bling? This is way, waaay too shady.
Maybe that's just what's trendy these days. Having a glowing collar helps those who comes feed it at night, too. Look at how dark its fur is. You gotta look really carefully to even spot it.
A dark-furred cloudbeast with a glowing collar and a fixed routine... Someone feeds it every night... Strange marks, strange sounds, and a component stuck inside the guy's air purifier...
Hah, what did I just say? I found the guy who's been tailing Mr. Lau!
Oh?
Take a look at the picture. That guy downstairs is holding something in his hand, looking up!
He's probably just looking at Siumi.
But Siumi's hanging out on Mr. Lau's windowsill?
Which means... that guy downstairs is using Siumi to eavesdrop on, no, to monitor Mr. Lau! That flashy collar? That might just be a camera!
Good thing you didn't mention this theory in Mr. Lau's place. He'd be scared out of his wits.
Did you see the bags under his eyes? He probably hasn't had a good night's sleep for a week. At this rate, he'll end up with neurasthenia.
Life in Lungmen's not really all that hard. I mean, Lee often gets himself dragged into some pretty hot messes... and there are things you can't talk over.

But the way I see it, if everyone just treated each other with sincerity and respect right from the start, things wouldn't be nearly as troublesome. If it's all a misunderstanding, then there's still room to talk things out, and it's always worth a shot.
After all, all this boils down to interpersonal problems. You don't like me, I don't like you. You envy me, I envy you back. It's a vicious cycle.
In any case, once we take care of the problem at its source tomorrow, Mr. Lau's worries will be a thing of the past.
Not every day we actually agree with each other...
Yeah, let's take care of the problem at its source. Heh, tomorrow, I'm gonna hit up the mastermind's crib and see exactly what it is they're up to.
Crib? What crib?
Phew… Let's head on home already. Gotta get up early tomorrow for work.
Where's Aak? I thought we were going to take care of this problem first thing in the morning.
Eh, whatever. I can probably handle this alone. I should be able to keep up appearances by myself.
Hello? Oh, Mr. Lau. I'm at the store.
Thanks for doing all of this. I'm almost done picking out everything I'll need.
Oh, right... Would it be okay if we got a small advance payment?
Hey, hey... Siumi, come on out.
You see this piece of meat? It's from my cup noodles this morning. If you want it, you gotta give me something in exchange—
Got it!
Hah, just as I thought. There's a camera on the collar's tag.
That's way too roundabout for gangs these days, using stray animals... If not them, then maybe some corporation? Or maybe it's a personal grudge thing?

Mr. Lau said he offended somebody... Maybe this is—
Hold up, is that the guy who was feeding Siumi downstairs last night? He's knocking on Mr. Lau's door.
Nobody's here. Hm, guess Hung stopped by and lured him away. Good one.
He's talking to somebody... Oh, is he leaving already? Not good. Gotta follow him. He might be trying to look for Mr. Lau.
Hey, outta the way, Siumi! I'm all outta meat!
Phew... He sure runs quick...
The shopping district? Shit, maybe he noticed I've been tailing him. It's the weekend. There's way too many people here! This isn't gonna be easy...
Huh? Is that... Hung and Mr. Lau? Why are they both holding all those bags? Those aren't their weapons or whatever, right?
Agh, what to do... Should I call the cops? But what if the L.G.D. takes Hung away too?
Whatever... Following that guy's more important.
Hey, coming through! Make way!
A residential building? That's pretty spartan for a crib...
Now he's got a huge bag in his hand. Most likely handed to him by one of his buddies from the shopping street... What's inside... Weapons? Stolen cash?
Argh, should I get in touch with Hung or call the cops first? He looks pretty thin, though. Bet Hung could take him down no problem.
Wait... Is he looking at me? Crap! He noticed me!
Ahhh!!! He's coming this way! And his hand is in the bag—
Uh, oh my, Wong... What happened to you?
Well, haha... I had a little fall last week and ended up in the hospital.
Goodness... That's pretty serious... Uh...
Mr. Lau and Mr. Wong simply look at each other quietly in embarrassment, as though the air in the staircase has frozen over.
Next to them, with a bright smile on his face and two plastic bags full of fruits in his hands, Hung looks toward Mr. Lau with expectant eyes.
(Whispering) You asked me where the coworker I reported lives, and this is why?!
(Whispering) Yeah!
(Whispering) You... You could've at least told me and let me prepare myself, mentally!
(Whispering) What? Didn't I say last night that misunderstandings between people ought to be resolved as soon as possible?
(Whispering) I didn't know you meant this—
May I ask what you two are here for? If you don't need anything, I'll head inside now.
Hold on, Mr. Wong! Mr. Lau has something important to tell you!
What do you mean?
It's really, really important!
(Whispering) Go on, Mr. Lau! We're here already. Might as well!
(Whispering) A-Alright...

Well, uh, remember how I got a little hotheaded last week and reported you? You see, for the last six months, work hasn't been going very smoothly, but you got promoted so easily... and I got a little jealous.
I really should've talked to you about this ahead of time! I mean, the company dealing in shady business doesn't have anything to do with me personally. I didn't have to stick my nose into this...
So, what I'm saying is, I'm here to apologize today, Wong. Please, take these!
Lau finishes getting everything off his chest, and hands the two big bags of fruit to Wong.

Wong's mouth is half agape, as though he just heard the most shocking news of the century. He already has one hand busy holding a crutch, and is unsure how to take the two bags of fruit with his free hand.
